problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(2i-4j)\,\text{m},$ with an acceleration of $(-i+j)\,{\text{m/min}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(3i-j)\,\text{m/min}.$ Find the distance from the particle to the origin after $6$ minutes.

feedback.problem:
A cyclist begins at the position $(2i-j)\,\text{m}$ with an initial velocity of $(3i+j)\,\text{m/s}$ and an acceleration of $(i+2j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$ Find the distance from the cyclist to the origin $(|r|)$ after $2$ seconds.

$\,|r|=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m}$
feedback.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=2i-j,\,u=3i+j,\,a=i+2j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the cyclist after $t=2\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(2i-j)+(3i+j)(2)+\frac{1}{2}(i+2j)(2)^{2} \\  & =(2i-j)+(6i+2j)+2(i+2j) \\  & =(2i-j)+(6i+2j)+(2i+4j) \\  & =(10i+5j)\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the cyclist to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|10i+5j| \\  & =\sqrt{{10}^{2}+{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{100+25} \\  & =\sqrt{125} \\  & =5\sqrt{5}\,\text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$
